pairs.difference: A: the cream envelope is a muted rest area, the green ground is loud, and the many-hued photo stays contained inside the envelope, like the real map and suitcase cards. B: the bat is a single violet mass on yellow-orange rings. Almost nothing but purple survives in the lens, warm_share is 0.825 and the shadows lose chroma (0.632). A's shadow value is also high at 1.605, so the numbers are not one-sided.
pairs.fix: Give the bat some muted body colors: dusty grey-brown fur on the body and a duller plum wing skin. Keep the ring background a softer yellow, and let the wing shadows stay rich deep purple.

pairs.difference: A: a near-neutral charcoal pot and grey-violet rock sit on a pure magenta wall, with acid green limited to the brew. Subject chroma is 0.056, hue families 2.03 and shadow chroma 0.493, all below the real range, so the wall carries all the color. B: blue shoes with green and pink trim on orange and cream have many accents (5.49 families), but the hero is as colorful as the ground, which is the balance real cards show.
pairs.fix: Paint the iron pot with a deep blue-green sheen and purple reflections in its shadows. Calm the magenta wall to a softer plum, and keep the green brew as the one bright accent.

pairs.difference: A: green topiary on a blue sky with a neutral pale curb and path. It is a simple, cool, natural-green arrangement, though warm_share is at the bottom of the range. B: every pumpkin is the same pushed saturated orange under a pink-magenta sky, with yellow-green grass and a red-brown fence. Subject chroma is 0.156, above the real range, and there is hardly any neutral anywhere to rest the eye.
pairs.fix: Vary the pumpkins with duller tan and ochre patches and darker burnt ribs. Make the sky a pale soft blue with white clouds, and mute the grass and fence.

pairs.difference: B is the same suitcase card shown in the real reference sheet: orange-brown case, multicolor stickers, green floor. A: cream column, crimson-plum wall, orange plinth and gold plaque all lean warm. warm_share is 0.962, far above the real range, and even the stone's shadows turn brown-mauve with no cool relief.
pairs.fix: Make the column a cool pale grey-white marble with blue-grey shadows. Set it against a cooler muted teal or slate wall, and keep gold on the plaque only.

pairs.difference: A: the grey-beige stone is nearly hueless at 0.042 subject chroma, below the real range, while the sky-blue wave background carries the color. warm_share is 0.041 and shadow chroma 1.453, both outside the range, with shadows going olive from moss and grass. B: green slide, blue ladder, yellow deck and pink ground have clear hero-versus-background hue roles and sit in range on every field.
pairs.fix: Tint the stone with visible warm and cool color, such as bluish lichen patches and warmer sunlit tan faces. Make the shadow side a clear blue-violet rather than olive.

pairs.difference: A: red body, green grass, cyan rings and black tires give clearly separate roles. Its low warm_share and shadow value (0.406) outside the range are explained by the black rubber and large cyan area. B: straw, handle and floorboards are all the same orange family, so hero and floor merge into one warm mass in the lens, with only a flat teal behind. The numbers favor B, so this is a weak call based on hue roles alone.
pairs.fix: Make the straw a paler natural wheat yellow and the handle a darker brown. Change the floor to a greyed cool wood so the broom separates from the ground by hue.

pairs.difference: A: pure cyan sky, lemon moon, glowing yellow windows, violet-brown walls and lime grass make 6.25 hue families at full loudness. The muted mauve masonry is the only rest area. B: blue door, orange frame, green ivy and a wreath with small bright accents have a clearer single hero hue and a cream wall as neutral. The numbers do not separate these cards, so the call is low confidence.
pairs.fix: Lower the sky to a dusky muted blue-violet and make the moon a pale cream. Keep yellow windows as the one accent, and dull the grass.

pairs.difference: A: an orange pumpkin on a pure violet burst, with background chroma of 0.252, above the real maximum and louder than the hero at 0.173. The fruit reduces to two flat loud masses in the lens. B: tan jacket, green sash and burnt-orange cuffs have real muted neutrals and an in-range green ground, so hero and background are balanced.
pairs.fix: Calm the purple burst to a softer, greyer violet. Give the pumpkin duller ochre and brown-red areas in its ribs, keeping the glow on the carved face.

pairs.difference: A: orange wall, red-brown wood, and a lavender-blue orb with a lilac-tinted stand. Warmth seeps into the table and metal, and the ground is lowest in chroma at 0.139. B: saturated blue cabinet on violet with tiny multicolor cans. warm_share of 0.026 is low, but the blue-on-purple hue role is clean and comparable to real blue or purple grounds. This is a thin call.
pairs.fix: Make the stand a neutral cool silver with no lilac tint. Change the wall to a clean muted teal or blue and the table to a less red brown.

pairs.difference: A: the coffin's wood and even the stone floor collapse to one red-orange-brown family with 2.29 hue families, below the real range. Grey paving turns brown in the lens and only the green stripes break it. B: yellow-orange chair and floor against blue with a lime cushion accent gives a clear, in-range complementary role.
pairs.fix: Paint the floor stones in cool blue-grey with no brown. Add a darker, less red wood with some muted olive-brown variation, and keep brass as the one accent.

pairs.difference: A: pure gold and cream on cyan is a strong complementary pair, and all fields except the low hue count are in range. B: the dark green iron lamp sits on teal in the same hue family, so the hero nearly loses its hue role. Subject chroma is 0.064 and shadow chroma 0.543, both below range, and the glass turns the same teal-green in the lens.
pairs.fix: Paint the lamp in warm dark bronze with brown-gold highlights so it contrasts with the teal. Make the glass a clear warm amber glow.

pairs.difference: A: four clean balloon hues on a slightly quiet blue sky with neutral clouds. Hue count is 5.45 and background chroma 0.107, slightly out of range. B: orange hull and off-white sails on a pink-violet burst over blue sea, with 6.23 hue families, also over range. Both cards show natural whites and comparable loudness, so color gives no reason to choose.

pattern: Generated cards still give themselves away through hue roles, not just raw loudness. One pushed family, usually orange or a warm mix, spreads across the hero, floor and even materials that should be neutral. Stone and wood shift brown, and whites shift cream. Otherwise the background is a pure, high-chroma field louder than the hero, or the hero is a single flat mass with near-neutral or thin shadows and no muted local color. Real cards keep cool neutrals and greys, clear hero-versus-ground hue separation, and shadows that stay related but varied. Caveat: the measured fields overlap heavily, so several calls here rest on small differences.
